assessment.nobel_worthiness: A poetic project that reworks Arabic verse through myth, fragmentation and sustained argument with the inherited tradition (Songs of Mihyar the Damascene; A Time Between Ashes and Roses). The linguistic and formal ambition is high, and the essayistic work on tradition and modernity supports the poetry's intellectual depth. Over decades, the oeuvre has been central to how modern Arabic poetry is understood.
assessment.attribution: A single poet-essayist. A citation would cover the renewal of Arabic poetic language and form, with the critical prose as a secondary strand. The scope is clear and attributable to one writer.
assessment.maturity: The career spans many decades and the body of work is long-established. The best-known collections are mature and widely discussed, so the timing is not premature.
uncertainties: Much of the poetry's effect lies in Arabic prosody and diction, which I can judge only partly through translation.
I have not independently verified the corpus, and my knowledge of the later collections is thinner than of the canonical early ones.
The relative weight of poetry versus essays in a citation would need to be settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visionary, densely patterned prose (Blinding; Solenoid) builds an expansive metaphysical project from memory, body and dream. The voice is distinctive and the formal construction ambitious. The imaginative depth is considerable, and the work draws on a poetic background.
assessment.attribution: One writer working in Romanian, across fiction and poetry. A citation would most naturally rest on the large-scale prose cosmology, with the poetry as a supporting strand.
assessment.maturity: A substantial, coherent body of work with sustained quality from the 1980s onward. The major novels are already recognized as a mature achievement.
uncertainties: The density and sentence-level music of the prose may not carry fully in translation.
The very long, recursive forms make it hard to judge consistency across the whole oeuvre from partial familiarity.
I cannot independently verify the full publication record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dreamlike, anti-realist fiction destabilizes psychology, space and causality, and the voice is unmistakably her own. The work is formally radical within Chinese-language fiction and has an intellectual affinity with Kafka-line experimentation and philosophical narrative. Her fiction asks serious questions about the limits of narrative sense.
assessment.attribution: A single fiction writer working in Chinese, with the stories and novels forming one continuous experimental project. A citation would concern formal invention and imaginative depth.
assessment.maturity: Active since the 1980s, with a large and consistent body of work. The method has stayed recognizably coherent, though the consistency may also limit its range.
uncertainties: Evaluation depends heavily on translations, and the coverage of her large output in English and other languages is uneven.
It is hard to separate the strongest works from repetitive variations without comprehensive reading.
Critical reception of her philosophical claims is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large polyphonic novels (Carpentaria; The Swan Book) remake the novel through Indigenous oral forms, sovereignty and ecological time. The ambition is great and the narrative language inventive. The significance rests on literary form and not only on subject matter.
assessment.attribution: One writer working in English. A citation could cover the renewal of the novel through Indigenous storytelling and polyphony, with nonfiction as a secondary area.
assessment.maturity: A relatively compact body of long books, but each is substantial and formally ambitious. The oeuvre is still developing, which is an argument both for and against timing.
uncertainties: Fewer major works than some other candidates, so depth across the whole body of work is harder to establish.
I cannot independently verify the reception of her most recent publications.
The relation between English-language text and the oral traditions it draws on is difficult to judge from outside.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large poetic sequences (Purgatory; Anteparadise) turn suffering and collective memory into monumental poetic form, including landscape-scale interventions. The voice is distinctive and the formal ambition high. The work holds a sustained position in modern Spanish-language poetry.
assessment.attribution: One poet writing in Spanish. A citation would concern poetry that gives collective historical suffering a new lyric and visual scale. Distinguishing the literary work from the performative and visual interventions requires care.
assessment.maturity: Long career from the late 1970s, with continuing sequences. The oeuvre is well developed.
uncertainties: Poetry in translation loses much of its sonic structure, which is central to Zurita's method.
Some of the most celebrated gestures are non-textual, and their status as literature is debatable.
Political context must not substitute for literary assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hybrid works (Autobiography of Red; Nox) recast the boundaries between classical scholarship, lyric, narrative and visual form. The voice is distinctive and the formal inventiveness real. The intellectual depth rests on engagement with Greek and Latin literature.
assessment.attribution: A single writer in English, across poetry, essays, translations and hybrid forms. A citation would rest on the formal reinvention of the book and the lyric essay.
assessment.maturity: A substantial body of work over decades, but the oeuvre is somewhat more varied and less unified than the strongest candidates.
uncertainties: Relative weight of the scholarly and translation work against original poetry is unclear.
Sustained quality across the whole output is harder to assess than for the top-ranked writers.
The material and visual aspects of her books are hard to evaluate in summary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dense, compressed prose (Small Lives; The Eleven) turns obscure lives and art history into narrative inquiry of high stylistic intensity. The linguistic achievement is notable, and the voice stands apart in French fiction.
assessment.attribution: One writer working in French. The citation would concern stylistic concentration and the reimagining of lives in prose.
assessment.maturity: A deliberately small oeuvre, with sustained quality in each book. The limited volume makes the argument from breadth weaker, though depth is strong.
uncertainties: The syntax and register are very hard to render in translation.
The narrow range and small number of books may weigh against significance across a body of work.
My knowledge of recent publications is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A long fictional career recovers divided histories through layered voices and varied social worlds (The Guest; Mater 2-10). The narrative range is wide and the imaginative engagement with modern Korean history sustained. The work draws on shamanic and oral storytelling modes in some books.
assessment.attribution: One novelist writing in Korean. A citation would concern the narrative recovery of divided history and marginal lives.
assessment.maturity: Decades of work with a large body of fiction. The scale suggests maturity, though quality across all the books is uneven in my understanding.
uncertainties: Biographical and political circumstances are significant but cannot count as literary merit.
Translation coverage of the full oeuvre is partial, and I cannot verify which works are available to the committee in each language.
Distinctiveness of voice is harder for me to judge in translation than structure and theme.
